chapter.title: Memory
chapter.para: Each partition runs in a memory space of its own. The requirements of this chapter state how the spaces are laid out and what the kernel checks when it touches memory of a partition.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_001
section.para: JetOS shall give each partition a memory space of its own: its code and data, its heap and the stacks of its processes, backed by physical memory that no other partition has.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Spatial partitioning is the basis of the isolation of partitions.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test and analysis.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_002
section.para: JetOS shall enable the memory protection of the processor (paging on x86_64, the MMU on arm64) before any partition runs, and shall run the partitions in the unprivileged mode of the processor.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Without both, a partition could reach the memory of the kernel or of another partition.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Analysis and test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_003
section.para: JetOS shall not let a partition read, write or execute the memory of the kernel or of another partition; an attempt shall be handled as a memory violation error of the partition (see health monitoring).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A fault of one partition must stay in that partition.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_004
section.para: JetOS shall map a configured memory block, by its name, size, virtual address and kind of access (read-only or read-write), into every partition that is allowed to access it, and into no other; the same physical memory shall back the block in all of them.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Memory blocks are the way partitions share memory when the configuration says so.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_005
section.para: JetOS shall give a partition, on request, the address, the size and the access that it has to a memory block named in the request, and an error if it has no such block.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The partition has to find out where a block is mapped.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_006
section.para: JetOS shall check every address that a partition passes to a service: the area shall lie in the code, data and heap of the partition, or in its stacks; a service shall refuse a request with a bad area with an error and shall not touch the memory.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The kernel must not be made to read or write memory that the partition could not.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_007
section.para: JetOS shall accept as the entry point of a process only an address in code that the partition can execute.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A process must not start in data or in the memory of another space.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_008
section.para: JetOS shall allocate the stack of each process of a partition from the stack area of the partition, with the size given when the process is created, aligned as the processor requires, and shall give all the stacks back when the partition restarts.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Stacks come from memory that the partition owns, and a restart begins with all of it free.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_009
section.para: JetOS shall share with each partition an area at the start of its memory, which the kernel and the partition both access, in which they keep the state that the partition's library needs (such as the mode of the partition and the state of its processes and critical sections).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Some state is cheaper to read in the partition than to ask the kernel for.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Review.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_010
section.para: JetOS shall allocate its own memory only while it initializes, from a heap that starts after the kernel image and ends below the memory of the partitions, and shall never free it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: No allocation after the start means no failing allocation and no fragmentation during the operation.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Analysis.

section.title: SRQ_JET_MEM_011

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The old interface for drivers in partitions that need the physical addresses of their buffers.

formalpara.title: Verification
formalpara.para: Test.
